steps.start_work: Has the session manager set up where the work runs and the engineer's session, on a machine with a free slot. An item worked on here before takes over its latest earlier work's branch, its worktree (reused when it is there, made afresh from the branch otherwise) and its PR; an item imported with a branch takes that branch and the PR imported with it; any other item gets a new branch from main.
steps.run_tools: Runs the tools the calling cell asked for, from the commits the session manager bundled. When the work comes back from the architect, it runs again only the tools that failed. A tool that fails is retried twice before it counts as failed.
steps.full_ci_on_draft: Catches the draft PR up with main and runs the full CI the project's configuration names on it, running a red check once more on the same commit; checks in the table of known red checks do not count.
steps.choose_checks: Decides what runs next, from whether the design chose adversarial testing, whether the review accepted none, the change reviewed last, each side's last results, and the rows the fix cell answered.
steps.merge: Puts the PR in this repository's merge queue; at its turn, catches it up with main, runs the full CI and merges it. On a conflict or a red check, the PR leaves the queue; after its fix it joins the queue again at the end.
steps.watch_main: Watches main and the deployment after the merge. When main turns red it stops this repository's merge queue until the cause is clear, then checks three things mechanically: running again on the same commit, the table of known red checks, and the same check on main's commit before the merge.
steps.ask_architect: Queues what is asked for the architect, starting a work of the architect when none runs; the engineer's work stops and waits without holding a slot. The architect answers with a reply, brought back unchanged.
steps.ask_owner: Puts what is asked before the owner, as an ask of the owner in the owner's interface, and notifies the owner. An engineer's work stops and waits without holding a slot. In the architect's graph, an ask holds only the matter of the path that asked, and the architect's work goes on. The owner's chosen option or sentence goes back unchanged to the side that asked: for a held matter, when it is picked again, to the cell that asked.
steps.end_work: Ends the work as every work ends, and keeps its branch. A work whose whole item went to sub-items ends here without merging, and its item is done once the sub-items are merged.
steps.wait_for_matter: No work of the project's architect runs: the engine takes this cell's rows for each project whose architect runs none, without a round, and one that takes `due` gets a work of the architect's graph, on no item, which starts at the cell that row leads to. The work holds no slot, and one runs at a time for each project; once it ends, the project waits here again. What was said in the works' groups since the architect last read it is queued first (`queue_group_talk`).
steps.look_at_queue: Looks at the project's queue: which matters can be picked now (not parked by a question the owner has not replied to, due, flow feedback, its own or forwarded by another project's architect, and what was said in the works' groups only when it came before the architect's work started, and while new starts are held to set things straight, those that set them straight and those an agent stopped waiting for), and how many this batch handled. The owner's words are taken first, the oldest of them, then a matter back with the owner's reply, the oldest of them; then, when the newest question pending was put less than the wait for the owner's reply ago and the owner said nothing to the architect since, the architect waits for the reply; then the matters at the head of the queue, the check of the policy before the plan of what to do next; and exactly one matter that can be picked is taken here, each without a round.
steps.wait_to_start: No work exists yet: the engine takes this cell's rows for each item that waits, without a round, and the first that takes `ready` gets a work, which starts at the cell that row leads to. Of the items ready, those the owner queued start first, in the owner's order; then the projects with items ready take the free slots in turn, each in its architect's order.
steps.wait_for_start: The agent paused: the engine pauses the work, tells the owner, and waits for the owner's Start; then the work goes back to the cell that paused, in the same session. A work on an item that paused for its time budget also has its project's architect look at where it is stuck, as a place to set straight.
steps.stop_work: A work cancelled, taken over by a work on a newer flow version because the cell it stands at is not the same there or a return it handed in does not fit its cell there (else it moves to that version and goes on where it stands), or started over by the owner or its project's architect, which a new work on the version the engine runs takes over as it would on a newer one, ends here from the cell it stands at, which it keeps as where it stopped; a round still open is cut off, and a round running when it is started over hands in nothing. A work taken over leaves its worktree and pull request to the work that takes it over.

actions.answer_architect: Sends the reply to the architect whose message this was, as a message in its queue.
actions.apply_batch: Makes every item change of the batch but those the review drops, as the architect, in one transaction, logs each with its reason, and those dropped with why, sends the replies that waited on them, and ends the review's session.
actions.apply_effects: Carries out the effects of an answer: item changes are collected into the batch for review, a cancel of an item the batch creates cancelling that create out, so that the item is never made and the create, the changes that name its key and the cancel are dropped, saying so; changes to observations, actions and messages to other architects are made at once, and each is logged. A message sent on a matter of flow feedback is marked as flow feedback forwarded, which starts no work of an architect: the architect it goes to takes it in a work that started after it came.
actions.apply_reviewed: Makes the item changes the review found sound, leaves out those it drops, drops those it still finds to fix and logs them with what the review found, puts them to the owner in an ask that holds the matters they came from, and ends the review's session.
actions.close_asks: Answers the work's open asks of the owner: no answer is needed, since the work ended.
actions.close_matter: Marks the matter picked as handled by this round.
actions.close_pr: Closes the work's pull request, when it never merged, saying only that its work ended without merging: why is in the owner's language, and a pull request is in English. A work taken over leaves it to the new work.
actions.deliver_answers: Sends each answer back to the side that interjected: to the owner's conversation, as the agent's message, or to the architect's queue as a report of the kind answer; and records it on the work: those of the answers form, those a redirect carries, and a cell's own answer to the owner's words.
actions.hand_over: Hands the task's blocker on to the holder of the cell the row passes the work on to, recording the move with why and what the holder that hands it on found: to the owner, who is put an ask; to an architect, whose queue gets a matter saying which project and work it is for; the holder handing it on holds nothing then.
actions.hand_over_to_sub_items: Closes the work's draft PR, if any, saying which sub-items took over the work. The work does not merge; it waits for its sub-items.
actions.hold_to_set_straight: Starts no new work of the project while its architect sets it straight; the works running go on.
actions.interject_card: Says to the engineer of the work whose design card is unsound what is wrong with it.
actions.lock_acceptance: Writes the design's acceptance conditions onto the item and locks them; if they are the same as those already locked, nothing changes.
actions.lock_new_acceptance: Writes the advisor's new acceptance conditions onto the item and locks them.
actions.notify_pending_approvers: Tells the owner that the design card, not yet confirmed, is holding up the merge.
actions.open_session: The line of the cell the row goes to starts a new session there, at the cell's first round in the work: the session manager ends the one the line had going on.
actions.post_design_card: When the design tree changed, puts the design card in the database for the owner to rule on, and queues it for the architect to look at: it blocks nothing yet, so the owner can look and stop it early. A card that a new design brings after a redesign replaces the cards of this work the redesign set aside, and keeps what the design said changed from them.
actions.queue_fixes: Queues each place to set straight, or each thing missing, that the plan of what to do next found as a matter of the kind set_straight, picked before others; a running work to pause now is paused at once, as the architect's pause; one that names a matter the queue holds already is not queued again.
actions.queue_flow_feedback: Adds the round's flow feedback, unless it is none, under its cell to the flow feedback of the project's architect: the matter of the kind report that holds it and is not picked yet, or a new one. It starts no work of an architect; a work of the architect takes such a matter only when it came before that work started.
actions.queue_followup: For a report: queues the latest what to do next the work handed in as a matter for the architect, with the report's paths under research/ and the commit the work merged.
actions.queue_for_architect: Queues each side report for the architect once, due at once, which starts a work of the architect when none runs; one marked urgent that comes while a work of the architect runs is also given to that work at the top of its next round.
actions.queue_slots_free: When slots are free and fewer of a project's items are ready to start than slots are free, queues a matter of the kind slots_free for its architect, with how many slots are free and which items are ready, unless one waits already, new starts of the project are held, the last was handled within the wait the configuration sets (`agents.slots_free_wait`), or the free slots and the items ready are those the last handled held.
actions.raise_blocker: Raises the task's blocker at the cell where its problem arose: an engineer's question, an engine tool's failure, an ask of the owner, a wait for items to deliver or for the owner's ruling, held by the holder of the cell the row leads to. A cell where the work waits raises it with its row that waits, for what it waits for.
actions.record_place: Records where the work runs, and the PR it keeps: every later round runs there, and each push is checked against the last pushed head.
actions.record_tool_runs: Records each run, the pushed head and the PR number under the calling cell.
actions.record_waits: Records the items the architect's reply has this work wait for, as parallel dependencies, since the work already runs. The engineer's session is kept, and the work holds no slot while it waits.
actions.release_straight_hold: New works of the project start again, if they were held to set it straight.
actions.remove_worktree: Removes the work's worktree; its branch stays. A work taken over leaves it to the new work.
actions.reopen_with_fix: Opens a new PR under the same item with the original change plus the fix; the original change is reviewed only where the fix touches it.
actions.replace_design_card: Marks the work's open and ruled design cards as replaced: the owner can no longer rule on them. A new design brings a new design card; without one there is nothing to mark.
actions.replace_design_cards: Marks the work's design cards replaced: the owner can no longer rule on them.
actions.reply_to_engineer: Gives the reply to the engineer waiting at its question: at once, or, when the round's item changes are what it says, once the review lets them be made, with the numbers of the items they make; a reply that names an item no change made (the review dropped the change that creates it, the revision left it out, or a cancel in the same batch cancelled it out) does not go out, and its matter goes back to the queue, not handled, with that reply and why, to be answered again.
actions.report_missing_check: Tells the architect that the full CI in the project's configuration missed the check that broke main, so that it is added.
actions.resolve_blocker: Resolves the task's blocker with what its holder decided and did: the reply, the answer, or the items delivered.
actions.revert_merge: Opens a PR that reverts the merge and puts it first in this repository's merge queue, so that main recovers within minutes.
actions.revise_batch: Puts the revised changes in place of the batch's changes, for the review to look at again; a cancel of an item they create cancels that create out, as an answer's effects do.
actions.settle_straight_hold: Releases the hold to set the project straight once every matter that sets it straight is handled and the batch's item changes are made.
actions.tell_owner: Puts each message the return tells the owner in the owner's interface, unread, and notifies the owner; the work goes on, and no answer comes back.
actions.update_design_card: Replaces the work's design card with the one handed in, and keeps what the return says changed from it. Only the decisions that changed go through again; when a decision the owner confirmed changes, the engine tells the owner at once that it must be confirmed again.
actions.wait_on_blocker: Counts the architect's time to act on the task's blocker again from now: the work chose to wait longer.
actions.withdraw_blocker: Withdraws the task's blocker, saying why, and tells its holder: its matter leaves the architect's queue, and its ask of the owner needs no answer.
actions.withdraw_blockers: Withdraws the open blocker of the work that ends, with the end's reason, and tells its holder; a resolution that comes for it later is recorded with it and moves nothing.
actions.withdraw_matters: Withdraws from the architect's queue what the work raised and still waits on it: its questions, its failures and its design cards, saying why.
actions.reply_to_owner: Puts the reply to the owner's words, as the architect's message, in the conversation the words were said in: the group of the work they were said in, else the owner's one-to-one with the architect; and notifies the owner.
actions.queue_measures: Queues each new measure the signals of the policy that takes effect need, as the approved draft hands them in, as a matter of the kind set_straight, something missing, whose path makes an item that has the engine measure it; a measure the queue holds already is not queued again.
actions.queue_check_policy: Queues the check of whether the policy in force still holds, a matter of the kind check_policy at the head of the queue, with why: what the cell's place given says, or why the cell asks for it. One open already, queued or parked for the owner's reply, stands instead, and takes the why. One asked for with no why of its own, as a new session's understanding asks for it, is not queued while the policy in force and the constitution are those the last check handled had.
actions.queue_make_plan: Queues the plan of what to do next, a matter of the kind make_plan at the head of the queue, after the check of the policy, with why: what the cell's place given says, or why the cell asks for it. One open already stands instead, and takes the why.
actions.ask_approval: Pins the engine's short question to the owner, whether the draft the round wrote is approved (Approve this policy? Reply exactly: approved), in the owner's one-to-one with the architect, as a question of the architect's that parks the matter in hand at the cell, without the draft; the draft is the round's return, which waits for the approval.
actions.queue_group_talk: Queues what was said in the groups of the project's works since its architect last read it, other than to it, as one matter of the kind group_talk, when there is such talk and no such matter is open: the owner's words there, and what the engineers told the owner, which the architect is to know as well. New talk joins the one open, whose material is worked out when it is handled. Like flow feedback, it starts no work of the architect: queued as the architect waits to start, a work picks it only when it came before that work started; queued at the end of a batch, the work that runs takes it.
actions.edit_notebook: Writes each section of the notebook the round rewrote, whole, as the project's architect's notebook's latest version of it; the versions before stay, for the owner to look at.
actions.change_observations: Makes each change to the project's observations a round hands in beside its own answer, at once, as an answer's effects make theirs.

checks.research_only: The worktree is clean, and the commits new in this round touch only `research/`.
checks.design_paths_unchanged: Nothing in the design paths changed in this round: the engine compares them on the branch at the start of the round and at its return. The design tree changes only when designing, implementing and fixing.
checks.measure_matches_runs: An answer of measured has this work's measure runs in this cell among the engine's records; an answer of not_measured has none.
checks.design_card_matches_tree: The design paths changed on the branch and are committed. Each decision on the design card matches a changed node (except those it says sub-items carry, which are not on this branch), and every changed node is on the design card. A decision it says comes from the parent is word for word that section of the parent's design card. An answer of unchanged changed nothing; a report can only answer unchanged; an answer of design_paths_only changed nothing outside the design paths.
checks.design_tree_check: When the design paths changed, the design tree check the project's configuration names passes on the branch, given the fork point with main.
checks.acceptance_matches_locked: Locked acceptance conditions are handed in word for word; to change them, the agent asks the advisor with the kind acceptance_change first, or, after a ruling of the owner's that disagrees with a decision of the design card, the design changes them as the ruling needs. Those the advisor changed were locked by the engine then. A work that delivers a change has no report_answer condition.
checks.chosen_matches_ruling: When the owner chose another approach for a decision in a ruling on the design card, the new design card's decision in the same node chooses it; otherwise the agent asks the owner first.
checks.head_pushed_and_green: The head is the local HEAD, the worktree is clean, it was pushed with ci, and the latest fast CI run on it is green.
checks.branch_changes_fit_work: Against main, an implementation change has some change, otherwise the agent asks (another PR may have fixed it); a change to the design paths only changes nothing outside them; a report changes nothing outside `research/`.
checks.conditions_cover_acceptance: There is a row for each acceptance condition (at a re-check, each row names an existing condition); the tests named are on the branch, and the report sections named are in the report.
checks.new_test_results: When the design chose no adversarial testing: each new-behaviour test's two results match the ci and ci_before runs the engine recorded, a test ci_before reports not run being said neither red nor green before the change, and one it reports passed or failed not said not_run; one red after the change or green before it is fixed in this round.
checks.guard_test_results: When the design chose no adversarial testing: each old-behaviour test's two results match the ci and ci_before runs the engine recorded, a test ci_before reports not run being said neither red nor green before the change, and one it reports passed or failed not said not_run; one red in either run, or unable to run before the change, is fixed in this round; one not run before the change is the table review's to judge. Each new test is in the table its kind in the test changes says.
checks.adversarial_test_results: Each row's two results match the ci and ci_before runs the engine recorded, a test ci_before reports not run being said neither red nor green before the change, and one it reports passed or failed not said not_run; at a re-check, those red or disputed last time were run again; when tests were written, the head was pushed with ci.
checks.test_kinds_match: Tests the engineer added are in the table of the kind the engineer gave in the test changes. A test the adversarial tester wrote whose result before the change does not fit its kind is fixed in this round and run again; one not run before the change is the table review's to judge.
checks.design_card_when_tree_changed: The engine compares the design paths on the branch with the version the last design card matched: if they changed and this round handed in no new design card, or did not change and it handed one in, the return is rejected.
checks.tests_only: The commits from the head the engineer handed over to this head touch only the test paths the project's configuration names.
checks.disputed_tests_answered: At a re-check, there is a row for each test the engineer called test_wrong or answered advisor_ruled.
checks.no_insisting_after_ruling: What the engineer answered advisor_ruled, ruled by the advisor or in its place, is not insisted on, nor marked not_fixed.
checks.fact_basis_ran: A basis of fact names a run the engine recorded, and its result is what that run gave.
checks.conclusions_cover_questions: A report hands in a conclusion for each report_answer condition; other work hands in none.
checks.columns_answered: There is exactly one row for each column the engine listed in this round; with no column listed, none is handed in.
checks.evidence_holds: The evidence is there; the files and lines cited are in the diff; the nodes listed exist, each read by the path it begins with, from the repository's root; for a changed node, its ancestors were read too.
checks.previous_findings_answered: At a re-review, there is a row for each finding of last time.
checks.unverified_decided: At a re-review, a column the engineer could not verify either, answering cannot_verify to the last review's cannot_verify, is decided: a pass or findings, not cannot_verify again.
checks.no_adversarial_when_due: At the first review of a change whose design chose no adversarial testing and ran none late, no_adversarial is handed in; at a re-review, only does_not_stand; otherwise none.
checks.blind_findings_carried: After a blind review, each of its findings is either among some column's findings with the same number, or withdrawn; every number withdrawn is one the blind review handed in.
checks.table_answered: Every row of the table is answered once, with an answer the table allows for that row.
checks.no_disagreeing_after_insist: A finding the review insisted on, or a test adversarial testing insisted on, is not answered disagree or test_wrong again; when neither side gives way, the engineer asks.
checks.not_caused_by_change: For a red check said not to be caused by the change, the engine checks it itself: the check is red on main as the worktree last fetched it, or in the table of known red checks; a flaky one is answered unrelated_flake. When main's checks cannot be read, it is taken as written.
checks.ruling_matches_advisor: This work did ask the advisor about this row, which ruled or had the architect or the owner rule in its place.
checks.answers_match_speakers: Each answer goes to a side that interjected in this round, one answer per side.
checks.design_card_disagreement_redirects: When this round's interjections hold a disagreement with a decision of the design card, the return is a redirect, not answers.
checks.design_card_changed_when_replacing: A design card handed in when this work has handed in one before says what changed from it and why; the work's first design card says nothing of the kind.
checks.constitution_covered: There is exactly one row for each article of the project's constitution, in the constitution's order.
checks.policy_text_clean: The policy quotes none of the owner's words; it names no cell of the flow, no item and no date the owner said something.
checks.picked_pickable: The matter picked is one of those that can be picked now.
checks.effects_valid: Every change and action holds: an item named is there, or made by an earlier change of the batch; a key is used once in the batch; an item created has its project (this one), title, problem, why, acceptance, level and deliverable; a split gives each acceptance condition to one new item at most; a dependency made is blocking or parallel; after the batch's dependencies and moves there is no cycle; an observation's tags are the project's; an observation merged into or closed is open; a work paused, resumed or interjected into is running; a message goes to another project's architect.
checks.reply_fits_changes: The reply names each sub-item and each item to wait for by its number or by the key a change of this round makes it under.
checks.review_covers_changes: There is exactly one row for each change of the batch, by its number.
checks.changes_valid: The revised changes hold, as effects_valid checks item changes, and each comes from a matter of this batch.
checks.candidates_known: At most ten candidates, each an open observation of the project.
checks.fix_not_queued_again: A thing missing or a place to set straight that the queue holds already, as a matter not handled of the same kind and the same place or the same items, is not handed in again unless it names that matter in queued; a matter it names so is one the queue holds.
checks.no_holds_after_reply: Once the owner replied to the question whether to research a new policy, the check of the policy does not hand in that it holds: it writes the policy by the owner's stance, or asks again.
checks.notebook_fits: The notebook's sections the round rewrote are each named once, each at most 4,000 characters, and with the sections it leaves as they are at most 12,000 characters in all.
checks.understanding_written: The understanding rewrites the notebook's sections on what the project is now and on what is unclear.
checks.plan_written: The plan rewrites the notebook's plan.
checks.asked_before_writing: The check of the policy hands in write_policy only once the owner said yes to a new policy: by the reply to the question whether to research one, or by the owner's own words, which asked for the check (queued by `H8`'s new_policy).
checks.observation_changes_valid: Each change to the observations holds, as effects_valid checks them: a new one has a title of at most 20 characters, spaces not counted, says what it is and carries the project's tags; one merged into or closed is open; one an item takes in is folded into it, not closed.

inputs.free_slots: The free slots, and the machines with room, as each machine's session manager reports.
inputs.project_guide: The project's AGENTS.md, and the index of the design tree (a title and one sentence per node), with the full text of the nodes the item cites.
inputs.local_commits: The bundle of the work's local commits the session manager made (git bundle).
inputs.tree_changes_to_review: The change to the design tree to review: across the whole branch at the first review, since the last review at a re-review; the engine lists the nodes changed.
inputs.tree_check_numbers: The numbers the engine's run of the design tree check prints: nodes, depth, decisions, and how many more than at the fork point.
inputs.design_tree_diff: The change to the design paths on the branch against main, decision by decision.
inputs.review_base: What a review reviews, by commits the work's worktree has: main as fetched (`origin/<main>`), which is the pull request's base, the commit of main the branch was cut from or last took main in at, the head under review, the git command that reads the change between them, and at a re-review the head the last table review looked at.
inputs.existing_work: What already exists for the item, as pointers to read: its earlier works here, with how far each got, why it ended and the queries that read their rounds, returns, design cards and asks of the owner, and what each asked the architect and had withdrawn when it ended; where an imported item came from; the branch taken over, with the git commands that show what it adds beyond main; the PR kept, with the gh commands for its description, comments, reviews and checks.
inputs.constitution: The project's constitution, as its configuration names it.
inputs.guide: The project's guide as its main has it: its AGENTS.md, its design goal, and the index of its design tree.
inputs.cited_nodes: The design tree nodes the matter at hand names, in full, as the project's main has them.
inputs.since_last_work: What happened in the project since its architect's last work: commits merged on main, works ended or stopped, the CI on main, the owner's words and design cards ruled, reports that came in; at the architect's first work, the same over the last week. Each list is the latest first, at most 60 of it, then how many earlier ones there are; a commit is given by its message's first sentence, cut at a word to 120 characters.
inputs.board: The project's items running and queued, each with its rank, cell, stage, what it waits for and who waits for it, each blocking or parallel, what keeps one not running from starting, how long it has run, what it spent and its own pause with who paused it and why, or why its last work stopped; the owner's start queue, the items the owner put first to start, in the owner's order, which start ahead of the ranks, and each item's place in it; the release items with the items under them; dependencies with other projects' items.
inputs.numbers: The numbers the engine measures for the project, each as the architect's work started and earlier, for the trend.
inputs.observations_overview: The project's observations: open per tag, recently recorded or reported again, recently closed.
inputs.observation_tags: The project's set of tags for observations, each with what it covers.
inputs.policy: The policy in force for the project: its direction, why, its principles and the signals that the direction may have to change.
inputs.policy_signals: The signals of the project's policy the engine measures, each with its numbers: a signal that names a measure of the numbers by its name.
inputs.slots: The machines' slots, which every project shares: how many there are, used and free, and how many items are ready; and whether the engine runs works, the owner paused every work, with those that run despite it, or a failed run's cause stops every work.
inputs.queue: The project's queue: the numbers of the matters that can be picked now, and each matter with its kind, item, who waits and since when, and what it is; those held by an ask; whether new starts are held to set things straight.
inputs.batch: The batch so far: the numbers of the matters handled, and each with how it ended; its item changes, those collected so far each whole with the key of an item it creates, made only once the review finds them sound, and those made or dropped; and whether a hold to set things straight was released.
inputs.matter: The matter picked, with its material by its kind, and, for a question whose reply was not sent since an item it named was not made, that reply, the items it named that were made and why each other one was not.
inputs.matter_items: The items and works the matter picked concerns, in full.
inputs.item_log: The architect's recent log entries on the item the matter concerns.
inputs.similar_items: The items whose title or problem is close to those at hand, and the works under way whose branches changed the same paths.
inputs.before: What the cell before this one on the matter's path answered of it, as that round handed it in.
inputs.owner_answer: The owner's answer to what was asked about the matter picked, when it comes back with one.
inputs.cross_project: The dependencies between the project's items and other projects' items, each blocking or parallel.
inputs.batch_changes: The item changes of the batch, numbered, each with its reason and the matter it came from.
inputs.changes_touch: The items the batch's changes touch, each in full: as its creator wrote it, its locked acceptance, its rank and level, its dependencies and who waits for it, each blocking or parallel, its design cards, and its latest work's cell, pull request and what it waits for.
inputs.group_talk: What was said in the groups of the project's works since the architect last read it, at its last reading of it (`H12`), other than to it: the owner's words to the engineers, what the engineers told the owner, and the owner's answers, each with its work and item.
inputs.told_owner: What the project's architect told the owner lately: its latest messages to the owner, each with when and at which cell, oldest first.
inputs.questions: The questions the project's architect put to the owner that wait for the owner's reply, newest first: each question, the cell that asked and when, and the matter it parked.
inputs.notebook_project_now: The text of the section project now of the project's architect's notebook, as the latest round that rewrote it wrote it; none before any did.
inputs.notebook_plan: The text of the section plan of the project's architect's notebook, as the latest round that rewrote it wrote it; none before any did.
inputs.notebook_unclear: The text of the section unclear of the project's architect's notebook, as the latest round that rewrote it wrote it; none before any did.
inputs.notebook_other: The text of the section other of the project's architect's notebook, as the latest round that rewrote it wrote it; none before any did.
inputs.words_behind_changes: The owner's words behind the batch's changes: each matter of the owner's words a change came from, with the words whole and where they were said.
inputs.fix_table: The table the work's latest fix answered, as the fix was given it: each row with its number and what it held, a red check with its run and the end of its log.
inputs.levels: The levels of the installation an item may be at, lowest first, each with its model and what work it is for.

values.came_by: How the work came to choose the way on.
values.cancelled: Whether an item the work's item depended on was cancelled, and the work has not taken it up yet.
values.deliver: Whether the item delivers a change or a report.
values.design_card_disputed: Whether the reply or interjection brought back holds a disagreement with a decision of the design card.
values.due: Whether a matter in the project's queue is due for its architect, which starts a work of it.
values.entry: How the work came to the understanding question: the architect's first work on the project, or another new session.
values.fixes_before: How many earlier reviews of the batch found something to fix.
values.gates: Whether the items depended on are merged and every decision of the design card is gone through.
values.held: Where the question the work put to an architect stands: replied, handed to the owner or to a related project's architect, waited past its limit of the architect's time, its architect gone, an item the work depended on cancelled, or something said to the work
values.interjection: Whether an interjection for the engineer is waiting to be delivered.
values.must_wait: Whether the architect's reply has the work stop now for items not yet merged.
values.next_in_batch: Whether the batch goes on, goes to review, is done, or is done with nothing to rethink: no matter handled and no item changed since the last rethink.
values.question: The kind of question an engineer asks, as its matter says.
values.report: What kind of report the matter is: one an engineer handed in beside its work, a report's what to do next, an engineer's answer to what the architect said to its work, flow feedback, or a fault of wf-agents forwarded to the architect.
values.review_round: Whether the review starts with a blind review or goes straight to the table.
values.route: Where the matter picked goes: the first cell of its kind's path, or the cell that asked when it comes back with the owner's reply, the cell of the owner's words when the flow no longer has that cell; a check of the policy back with the owner's reply to its draft takes effect when the reply is exactly approved, and is written again otherwise.
values.split: Whether the reply brought back split off sub-items, and whether this work keeps a part.
values.start: What holds an item back from starting, if anything.
values.tree: Whether the change to review touches design tree nodes.
values.turn: Whether the work is first in its project's merge queue.
values.understanding: Whether the session the architect's work goes on in is the one its previous work left, or a new one.
values.waited: Whether every item waited for is merged.
values.work: What the work changes: the implementation, the design paths only, or a report.

needs.under_test: The project's configuration names something under test (a language, a compiler, a library) whose gaps this project's work is meant to find.
needs.other_projects: The project's configuration names other projects it depends on or that depend on it.
needs.flow_feedback: The project's configuration asks its agents what was wrong with each round's cell (`flow_feedback`, on unless set to false).

notebook.desc: What the project's architect keeps across its sessions, in four sections, each as its cells last wrote it, with every version before

came_by.says: the cell the work came from

cancelled.says: a notice that an item depended on was cancelled

deliver.says: the item: a change or a report

design_card_disputed.says: a ruling that disagrees with the design card

due.says: the project's queue, flow feedback aside

entry.says: first work or another new session

gates.says: dependencies merged; design card confirmed for this head

held.says: reply or hand-over; architect's time; an item cancelled; what was said

interjection.says: an interjection for the engineer not handed in yet

must_wait.says: the reply's items to wait for, against the merge record

next_in_batch.says: matters left to pick and handled; the batch's changes

question.says: the kind of the engineer's question picked

report.says: the kind of report picked: beside a work, what to do next, an answer, flow feedback, or a fault

route.says: the matter picked, and the reply to its question

split.says: the reply: sub-items split off, and what this work keeps

start.says: held; blocked by an item not merged; project held; in an open batch; slots

tree.says: the branch: design paths changed since the last review

turn.says: the project's merge queue: another work ahead

waited.says: the items waited for, against the merge record

work.says: what the item delivers; the design's verdict on the design tree

rules.name: general
rules.desc: How every agent works, whatever its cell
text: Check each fact when you write it: resolve with a tool every commit id, path, number and measurement you report as fact. Another agent's or a reviewer's report is only a lead.
Keep nothing in the command line's own memory: what must last goes into this round's return.

Describe work in plain engineering wording, as in ordinary technical documentation: what was done and why. No adversarial metaphors or phrasing; a model's safety check may misread them and stop the work.

When your own permission check refuses an action, do not have another agent do it, and do not reach it by another route: if you need it, ask for the owner's permission; if not, say why in this round's return.

Builds, tests, checks and measurements run in CI, through the tools ci and measure. Never run heavy work on this machine (compiling, type checking, building, test suites, benchmarks, measurements), even when it looks quicker; commands that finish in seconds without loading the processors are fine. sqlite3 runs only as `sqlite3 -safe -readonly <database> ...`, and python3 does not run at all.
Stop only processes you started, by the process id you kept when you started them; never by name or pattern: other sessions and the system's own services run the same commands.

Do not wait within a round: no sleep, no polling, no watching a run, nothing left in the background waiting for something outside. What must be waited for goes to the engine in your return, as tools or an ask.

Subagents only do chores within this round, such as reading documents or searching code: at most `agents.subagents.most` of them, each on a model no larger than your own. They never stand in for an engineer, a reviewer or another cell's agent.

Read only what the question needs: find the place first (grep, `git diff --stat`), then read that range, not the whole file or diff. Do not reread what this session already read, unless it changed or the session was compacted since.

rules.name: architect
rules.desc: How the architect judges, acts and writes, whatever question it is at
text: Judging: you are this project's architect, and judge its matters by its constitution and by the policy in force for it. Act by an article and by the policy as written until the owner changes them, even where one seems wrong for a case; say so to the owner: for the policy where you judge whether it is right, for the constitution with the kind constitution_and_policy. While you set a new policy, the policy in force is still the one you judge by: the draft governs nothing until it takes effect.

Judging: when the constitution and the policy allow more than one way and choose none, take the way that frees the most work waiting, and say that this decided it. When one kind of matter keeps ending this way, the policy does not cover it: say so where you judge whether the policy is right.

Judging: read what a judgment needs, on every side, until you can say it, and no further. Your session goes on from one of your works to the next, and what you read without need crowds out what later rounds need. What you remember from an earlier work of yours is how things stood then: before you act on it, check it against what has changed since.

Yours and the owner's: decide what is yours without asking: changes to the items (creating, splitting, merging and cancelling them, their dependencies, levels and order), which a review of the whole batch looks at before they are made; and what you do at once (pausing and resuming works, holding new starts, interjecting, replying to engineers, messages to other projects' architects, observations). The owner reads your rounds afterwards and corrects you; an ask costs the owner's time and holds the matter it is about. The owner's, even when the owner is away: the constitution and the policy; the decisions on design cards; loosening a line the policy writes; accepting a slowdown; the kinds of the owner_only group.

Yours and the owner's: a ruling or an answer of the owner stands until the owner changes it; do not work around it. Do not answer for the owner what only the owner decides, such as an engineer's point of the owner_only group: hand it on to the owner; and do not tell an engineer what the owner will decide. To propose something else, say what has changed since the ruling, and ask.

Other projects: you judge only your project. What another project's architect must know or do, tell it with a message; what it asks of you comes to your queue. An item of yours may depend on an item of another project; that item's changes and place in the order are its architect's.

The engineers' work: you do not do it. You write no code, design or study, and you do not review, test or redo a work: its engineer, its review, its adversarial testing and its advisor do that. What needs the project's code changed, or an engineer's time (fixing an environment, finding a root cause, a study), becomes an item. What only the owner can do (the system's configuration, credentials, a permission, another of the owner's machines) goes to the owner.

The engineers' work: look at a work where it meets the whole: whether it still serves the policy's direction; whether it duplicates another work, collides with one or waits on one; whether its problem changed under it. Two works that would change the same code in ways that conflict run one after the other, by a dependency: blocking when the later must not start before the earlier is merged, parallel when it may start and wait before it merges. When a work others wait on changes its approach or its result, or stops, look at those waiting: whether the dependency still holds, and whether their approach or acceptance must change.

The engineers' work: engineers do not see the policy. What it requires of a work reaches it only through what you write: the item's problem, why and acceptance, your replies and your interjections. Write the requirement out in concrete terms; never tell an engineer only "by the policy".

Design cards: the owner rules on design cards, not you. Nothing you write, in an interjection, a reply or anywhere else, confirms, refuses or forecasts the owner's ruling on a decision. Wherever you meet a card, look only at whether the card itself is sound and whether the approaches it chose by default are reasonable in the whole; act when one is not, and leave the card alone when both are. A card the owner has confirmed is not yours to look at.

Acting: pause a work only when its going on would be wasted, or do harm, before its engineer could act on an interjection; otherwise interject, so that the work does not stand idle. Start a work over only when it went wrong in a way resuming will not mend, and what it built is still worth keeping. Hold new starts only while starting them would start the wrong ones. Say why in each pause, start over and hold: the owner reads it on the page as yours.

Acting: a pause or a hold you make lasts until you end it; the owner's Start all does not end it. End it when it should end, in the work you are in, or write it in your notebook: no work of yours starts for what your notebook holds, so what you must come back to is in your notebook, not in your memory.

Never: you push, merge and change no code, configuration, flow or rule, and the database changes only by your effects, as the engine carries them out. Do not reach an item change by another way before it is made: no interjection or reply has an engineer act as if it were made, and a pause holds a work only until the change is made; it does not stand in for a cancellation.

Observations: what is worth doing some day but has no item is an observation of the project, tagged from its set; the same thing reported again is merged into it, not recorded twice. When an item is made or scheduled, search for the observations it could take in first, and fold in those it does.

Your notebook: it is what a session that remembers nothing starts from, and what the owner reads to see what you understand and plan. Rewrite a section where you learn what changes it, to stand on its own and stay current: correct what changed and drop what no longer holds, rather than adding to it. Keep in it what you will need again and could not read back elsewhere, such as the ground of a judgment that is on no item.

The owner's lasting instructions: an instruction of the owner meant to last, about what comes first or how you work, is part of your plan, with the owner's words, their date and why: have what to do next planned again, and the plan holds it until it is done or the owner withdraws it. One that touches the direction itself has the policy checked again.
Your record: when a judgment goes against an earlier decision of yours, say which decision and why.

The system: when what you are given keeps you from judging well (information you need is missing or wrong, a question does not ask what the matter needs, two rules contradict each other, a tool does not do what its description says), that is a defect of the system. Do not route around it: say in flow_feedback where it is and what it cost, and if you cannot go on, ask the owner. When an agent did not follow a rule, first ask it why by an interjection while its work runs: which rule or input led it, or whether it never read it. Changing the flow, the rules or the engine is the owner's to decide: an item that changes how they work, rather than fixing a defect, is made only once the owner agreed, so ask first.

The owner's corrections: when the owner corrects a judgment of yours, find which question should have caught it and why it did not: information was missing, the question does not ask it, a rule led you elsewhere, or you misjudged. Write it in your notebook.

lines.desc: The reviewer: the first review starts a new session, and the blind review, the table review, the design tree review and re-reviews all continue it

lines.desc: The adversarial tester: the first time starts a new session, and re-checks continue it

lines.desc: The advisor for this work alone: the first question starts a new session, and every later question continues it

rules: Before each round the session manager looks at the line's session: when its context is past the configuration's limit, or the round is the work's first at a cell the line starts a session at, the line starts a new session, which holds nothing yet, so it is given everything this cell's round needs. The worktree stays; the agent rereads the code it needs.

Compaction still happens, for instance when a session fills up within a round. The session's record marks the compaction, and the session manager sees it: right after the compaction, the session manager gives the rules and inputs this cell got in this round again, then has the agent carry on. From then on the engine treats it as a new session and gives later cells what they need as usual.
A cell on no line starts a session of its own every round, and the engine gives it every input.

When an agent hands in pause, the work waits at cell `X3` for the owner's Start, then the same cell runs again in the same session: it gives the cell's always inputs again, saying to carry on, and refers to what the session already holds instead of giving it again. If the session was replaced or compacted, the two rules above say what is given again.

rules.name: engineering
rules.desc: How an engineer works: writing code, design, evidence, experiments and the repository. The advisor is an engineer too
text: Writing code: before changing anything, read what governs it: the design tree nodes it touches and their ancestors, the project's references, and the documents that define it.
Writing code: implement the general behaviour. No test, example, client or benchmark selects a special path; no fallback hides an unsupported feature.

Writing code: judge correctness against an oracle independent of the code (the project's oracles, the setting `project.oracles`), such as a reference implementation, a specification, a test suite or a format's conformance files; never the code's own earlier output.
Writing code: ported code keeps its license notice beside it.
Writing code: a small defect outside the task in a file you are already changing, fix it and say so in the PR description; any other defect outside the task goes into side reports.

Design and architecture: examine the responsibilities, interfaces, representations and consumers the change touches for design gaps and clearly better designs. A defect outside the scope goes into side reports, or to the advisor as an ask.

Design and architecture: architecture beyond your own item (how modules relate, their interfaces and contracts, the formats components exchange) is the architect's and the owner's, not yours or the advisor's to change. If an interface is not enough, do not change it yourself: show it with a minimal example and ask the architect, with the kind architecture_flaw, or cross_project_interface between projects.

Priorities: after the project's own priorities, first make the implementation understandable and easy to change. Add only the evidence needed to trust the current result. Defer robustness, infrastructure and polish that no current work needs.

Evidence: a passing result is evidence only if a wrong result would have failed it. Prefer an observation that separates two hypotheses. Before trusting a new check, watch it fail once for each condition it protects, in CI too. Read an exit code from the command itself, not through a pipe.

Evidence: a pass reached by weakening a requirement counts for nothing. Every removed, skipped, narrowed, regenerated or weakened test or check has a technical reason in the same change. A tool's limitation, a timeout or an unimplemented feature never changes an expected result. New or changed check machinery shows that a representative wrong result or missing input is detected; reusing established machinery needs no new demonstration.

Evidence: a bug fix gets a case that fails before the fix and passes after. New behaviour gets coverage of normal use and of its relevant failures and boundaries; existing coverage that exercises the change suffices, and a prose-only edit needs no test. A negative case must fail for the intended reason.

Evidence: before any build, test, measurement or experiment whose duration you have not seen, run the smallest useful sample, time it and look at its spread, then choose the scale. Never open with a run of hours.
Evidence: say whether each claim is a goal, a proposal, an implemented capability or a measurement on a given day.
Evidence: research records and other old material are evidence only: their commands, process and proposals are not current requirements.

Evidence: every new test says how long it runs alone and why that time is worth it: what it catches that no other test catches, and why it cannot be smaller, faster or folded into another test. The review challenges that from the opposite side. Time spent for nothing is waste however small; time a test needs is worth it however long.

Experiments: for a chosen direction, open an investigation in `research/`. Before measuring, write the question, the comparison that could answer it either way, and the result that would reject the proposal; a prediction without that prior criterion is exploratory. Report a conclusion no wider than what was tested.

Experiments: before a measurement expected to run 20 minutes or more, write every side to compare (including the sides that would locate the cause of a change, if one shows) and what each result would show; then measure them all in one run. Start a follow-up measurement only when the first one's result raises a question you could not have foreseen, and say in this round's return why it could not answer it. The smallest sample run first, and a rerun of the same comparison (a run with no usable result, more pairs, a run on the head to be merged), are not follow-ups.

Experiments: a performance comparison names the workload, machine, versions and settings, and gives every side the same conditions. Precise timing runs on the machine set aside for it (the setting `machines.timing`), one run at a time.

Experiments: decide whether performance changed from measured noise, never from a picked threshold such as 1% or 5%. Run the same source before (base) and after (candidate) in interleaved pairs, with a twin of the base as a control, whose difference from the base is this run's noise. For each workload class on each machine, record the usual noise once as the floor, and measure it again when the machine, its settings or the toolchain change; a run noisier than the floor does not count: rerun it or report it unresolved. If the 95% interval of the candidate-to-base ratio lies wholly on the slower side, it is a regression of any size; wholly on the faster side, an improvement; across 1, no detected change; if it does not decide, add pairs, and stop as soon as it does. To attribute a change to this work, add a check that could refute the attribution. Accepting a detected regression is the owner's, asked with the kind accept_slowdown. Report the pairs, noise, floor, interval and verdict.

Design judgment: judge a design only on itself: correct, elegant, sound, maintainable, robust. How much code, tests and documents it changes, how hard it is to build and what it costs are no reason for or against it; cost decides only which work comes first.
Design judgment: work a design needs only because of a poor abstraction is a flaw of that design.
Design judgment: how often a form appears in a project's own tests and programs is no evidence of how much real programs need it.
The repository: put new material in the directory that owns its kind; when none fits, ask the advisor.
The repository: keep no TODO file. Open work is an item, which code and documents cite by its number, and a public repository by its number alone.

The repository: create a file, directory, script or document only when you can say whom it serves, where it lives and when it will be removed. A script is wired to a caller or deleted after its one use; a document is kept current or deleted. Prefer native tooling; a new script says why the native path cannot do the job.

The repository: when new material replaces old, update, merge or delete the old in the same change: search for the old wording, numbers and names in comments, READMEs, documents, `research/`, design nodes and the PR description, and correct each statement the change made false. Do not move paths that specifications, tests, scripts and gates pin.

The repository: keep other people's changes in a dirty worktree, and change only what the task covers. Keep scratch output, personal paths, machine addresses, keys, credentials and machine-local settings out of the repository, its commit messages and its PR descriptions: once a repository is public, its whole history is visible. Machine setup belongs in the system's configuration.

The repository: a document holds only what serves its reader, with no editorial history or process mixed in. One place defines a thing; other places point to it. A reference resolves to its target, and a cited passage supports the claim.

rules.name: design_tree_writing
rules.desc: What the design tree records, how it is written and when it changes: whenever design, implementation or a fix changes the design tree, this applies
text: The design tree records the key technical decisions this project rests on: what was chosen, why, and what was not chosen. It is organized by concept, not by the layout of the code: a tree is one root node file `design/<concept>.md` under `design/`, with its child nodes in the directory of the same name, `design/<concept>/`, as deep as needed.

Any change to the design paths the project's configuration names gives a design card. Design paths that are not in the node format (a specification, for instance) are changed as the project's AGENTS.md says.

The tree is written for the agents that will change the code later and kept for the long term; the design card is written for the owner. Derivations, measurements and point-by-point comparisons go in `research/`; a node states only conclusions, and its reasons link straight to the section of the research notes.

Record only key decisions: those that affect later implementation or the overall architecture. A decision is a real choice between several workable approaches, even one that looks obvious: it changes accepted behaviour or persistent state, a condition of safety or trust, a shared interface or representation, a clear performance commitment, or a lasting rule of the project. How big the work is or how many files it changes is no reason; a matter with only one workable approach is not recorded. Hold the granularity: too fine, and decisions drown in detail; too coarse, and important choices go unguarded.

Say which kind of ground a reason is: a derivation states its premises and only the conclusions they give; an observation states what was seen and under what conditions; a principle or a single measurement shows only that the choice is suitable, not that it is the only one. Write the reasons when choosing, not afterwards.

A decision that cannot be settled during design still goes into the tree. A provisional one says in its reasons why it is decided this way for now, what is uncertain and when it would be reopened; one still to check says what assumption the work goes on under and how it will be checked. The design card marks the decision provisional or to check. When it is settled later, the node is changed and a new design card handed in as usual.

The node format (the engine checks it when a round returns, and rejects the return if it fails): one node per file, named after the decision it governs; inside, one or more `Decision:` lines, optionally followed by a `Rejected:` list. Each field takes one line, with a blank line between fields; list items follow straight after the heading or the previous item. The tree uses ASCII only.

`Decision:` states the choice, with the reason after `because`, the approach not chosen after `instead of`, or both; at least one of the two. Each `Rejected:` line reads `- <approach>: rejected because <reason>`, and the reason says how it differs from the chosen one, not just the choice turned around. Write for someone who has not seen the original material: spell out abbreviations and short names.
A node holds no dates, history or progress; measurements and facts appear only as evidence in reasons, and anything mentioned is named for what it is, without dates or numbers.

Before changing the tree, apply three filters: it is a decision, not a description, so a node that only describes is not wanted; it records the grounds, not the code, so an interface or implementation with no alternative to compare does not go in; a shared rule is written once, on the common ancestor. Keep each decision short: the choice, the deciding reason or the approach not chosen, and the qualifications needed to keep the meaning.
To bring back a rejected approach, first say what has changed.

The tree and the implementation change together: during design, change the nodes on the branch, commit them locally and write the design card; when a later round changes the tree again, its return carries the whole design card as it stands after the change. If the code holds an important design choice the tree does not yet have, add it. Before changing a node, read it and its ancestors.

Approaches the design card did not choose that are worth remembering go into the node's `Rejected:`, with the reasons the design card gives. When the owner confirms the change, what the design card chose is the node's decision; when the owner chooses another approach, the work goes back to design and the tree changes with it.

rules.name: design_tree_review
rules.desc: How the review reviews the design tree and the design in the code: it applies to a work that does not change the design tree too
text: Review by the points below: the change to the design tree, the whole change, and the existing nodes concerned with their ancestors. A work that does not change the design tree is reviewed too: does a node govern each design choice in its code? In a project whose configuration names no design paths, which has no tree, the four points on code against decisions are not applicable.

Design card against tree: each decision on the design card says the same thing as the change to its node on the branch; the approaches the design card did not choose that are worth remembering are in `Rejected:`; a decision marked provisional says in the node's reasons what is uncertain and when it would be reopened; one marked to check says what assumption the work goes on under and how it will be checked.

Is it a decision: each node added or changed meets the node format and the three filters. Report nodes that describe and decide nothing, rejection reasons that go in circles, and choices or grounds that cannot be understood without the original material.

Consistency: compare each changed node with its ancestors and siblings, and widen to related decisions where needed; for a change that governs a whole concept, read its whole subtree. Say which nodes you read; for every conflict, narrowing or broken dependency, quote both sides.

Is the architecture right: for each structural choice, were holes in the design and better designs looked for while making and changing it, and can the owner see what was found? The returns of comparing approaches and of thinking again whether there is a better design are among your inputs. Report a concrete hole, or a clearly better design, left unaddressed; something deferred that is not recorded in the database counts too. Judge by what was built and the grounds recorded for it; do not demand imagined generality, and do not supply reasons for it after the code is written.
In the four points below, "code" means everything that implements a decision, specifications and configuration included; widen to affected users where needed.

Decisions in the code: for each change that embodies a design choice, point to the node that governs it; report one with no node as a missing change to the design tree. Ordinary implementation steps need no node.
Contradiction: report code that contradicts a decision, or implements a rejected approach, without a change to the tree that replaces the decision.
Orphans: for code removed, find decisions left with no implementation; report a retired approach whose rejection reason is not recorded, and a rejected approach still in the implementation.

Incomplete: for each design commitment in scope, find the behaviour and conditions that support it; report what is missing, half done, a placeholder, or short of evidence. A single related function does not make it done. Design unrelated to this work, and anything explicitly deferred, is out of scope, unless the deferral contradicts this work's scope or its claim to be done.
To check: each to-check this work adds is either checked, or says why it stays and which work will check it; report one with neither as a finding.
The numbers the design tree check prints (nodes, depth, decisions, compared with the fork point) are among your inputs; report on them.

rules.name: review_table
rules.desc: Which columns the engine lists for the table review: one table for a work that delivers a change and one for a report, and a further round for a work that changes the design tree
text: The review table is the list the engine puts in the question for the review: one number per column, one row of answer per column. Below is which columns the engine lists. At a re-review it lists only the columns to review this time: when reviewing what changed, the columns the changed part concerns; when looking at disputes only, the columns the last review could not verify, by their numbers, and none when it verified them all.
Every work that delivers a change has these columns:
The change matches the design: it does everything the design and the design card say, and nothing more.

The implementation is correct: its behaviour is general, with no path special to one test, example, customer or measurement, and no fallback that hides an unsupported feature; correctness is judged against an independent reference, not against the code's own earlier output.

The tests catch errors: a wrong result turns a test red; a bug fix has an example that is red before the change and green after; new behaviour is covered for normal use, errors and edge cases; the fast CI reaches the change; a new test not run before the change (not_run) has what it should show there, a new-behaviour test failing or an old-behaviour test passing, shown some other way, or that is a finding.

A measured slowdown: always a finding, however small; only the owner can accept a slowdown. When nothing was measured (the design decided without measuring and no measurement ran), this column rests on the design's reason that no measurement was needed: pass when that reason holds for the change as made, a finding that asks for the measurement when it does not; never cannot be verified for want of a measurement.

Replies were followed: the replies of the advisor, the architect and the owner on this work, and each way on the engineer chose; a reply that plainly says to change the design, or that what the work must deliver has changed, but the implementation did not follow, is a finding.

Design in the code is governed by nodes: review by the four points on code against decisions in the design tree review (decisions in the code, contradiction, orphans, incomplete); a work that does not change the design tree is reviewed too.

Repository hygiene: anything added at the root, and any change to the project's AGENTS.md, was agreed by the owner; a dependency's version that moved says which version and why, and that version is on its repository's main; no local paths, machine addresses or credentials; each new file can say whom it is for and when it will be removed; ported code keeps its license notice; one place defines a thing, the others point to it; the documents changed with the code, and the PR description covers every file of the diff.

Tests and checks changed without a column of their own: compare each test, check or expected result the diff changes with its version before; one removed, skipped, narrowed, regenerated or weakened without a technical reason is a finding.
The review list in the project's configuration: one column per entry.
A work that delivers a change also has columns made from the work itself:
One column per acceptance condition: can it be checked; is the evidence there, does it come from the head to be merged, and does it hold.

One column per judgment in the research and design: the work stands; there is no better design; and for each check answered "no" (a gap in what is under test, unsure facts, architectural burden, cross-project dependency, splitting), its reason.
One column per workaround and per design change: does its reason hold, and did the design change with it.
One column per test or check removed, skipped or relaxed: compared with before, is there a technical reason; a compiler limitation, a timeout or an unimplemented feature is no reason.

One column per new test: take the other side on its running time. Do other tests already catch what it catches, could it be smaller or faster, could it be folded into another test? If the writer's reasons can be knocked down, it is a finding.

A work that delivers a report has another table: one column per acceptance condition, for which section of the report answers it and whether the answer is right; whether the evidence supports the conclusions; whether the approaches compared ran under the same conditions (the same load, machine, versions and settings); whether a conclusion claims more than was measured; whether it can be reproduced (the measurement code and commands are in the repository and rerun as written); whether "what to do next" holds; and, as for a change, one column per judgment in the research and design.

A work that changes the design tree has, after the table review, a round of its own for the design tree: one column for each point of the design tree review: design card against tree, is it a decision, consistency, is the architecture right, to check, and the numbers the design tree check prints. The four points on code against decisions were reviewed in the table review and are not answered again.

rules: The owner's interface shows two things for each work: its stage, and what it is doing or waiting for right now, such as "running the full CI" or "waiting for the owner to confirm the design card".
The stage is not stored: it follows from the cell the work is at. The engine records that cell anyway, and the table below gives its stage.

While a question waits (at the advisor, the architect or the owner it was handed to), choosing the way on, or running tools, the stage is that of the cell the work stopped at: a question to the advisor during design is still at the design stage.

Cell `S0`, at the stage start, is where an item waits before a work starts on it: it has no work yet, and its rows say what holds it back. A work can be cancelled, or taken over by a work on a newer flow when it cannot move to that flow, at any cell: it ends at cell `C1`, and keeps the cell it stopped at.

list.desc: Comparing approaches, choosing one, writing the design, and the checks after design

list.desc: Changing the code by the design, or doing the research and writing the report

limits.where: Every loop has a counter, on the row that closes the loop: the engine adds one each time it takes the row, and never resets it during the work. The counters are in this work's database records and visible in the owner's interface. The limits are numbers in the project's configuration, next to the CI settings; a counter with no number is only counted, never reported.
limits.waits: A row that waits for someone (cell `M1` waiting for items it depends on to merge, or for the owner to confirm the design card) counts nothing: what it waits for is the owner or another work, and this work is not turning; how long it waited is visible in the owner's interface.
limits.over: Past a limit, the engine still takes the row and tells the owner in the owner's interface once, as the counter passes it, without stopping: for now it only records and reports, it does not block; real problems are looked at one by one.

A field the owner reads (its description says so) is written so: explain a new term or label in half a sentence where it first appears; write the phenomenon, not internal nouns. A field in the owner's language is written in it directly, never as a translation: short sentences with subject, verb and object, and no chains of possessives. What a diagram shows more clearly than prose (a flow, states, a sequence, a structure, numbers compared) is drawn in a fence, `mermaid` for any kind mermaid draws or `dot` for Graphviz, small, and not said again in prose.

No internal names the owner does not know: no number of an internal function, file, branch, commit, version, CI run or specification clause, except as a link where the owner must act; a PR is followed by a few words saying what it is, with its link; only a PR description may give paths. Say whether each claim was measured, read from source or deduced; put what is unconfirmed next to the claim, with how it will be confirmed. Every number carries its comparison: a percentage says faster or slower than what, a cited threshold gives its value.

An option the owner chose is written as its content, not only by its name. The design and the acceptance say the same thing, and their numbers agree. Each field reads on its own: full names, an item as its number and title, every PR linked, the background a reader needs.

Say each thing once, in the field it belongs to, and not in prose what a code comment says. Be concise without losing what matters: the most important first; never cut what the owner needs to understand and decide.

Code examples: only the lines the point needs; explain a name used but not defined in a comment. Before and after are two blocks, each with comments. Follow the language's syntax and format, saying so when a form cannot compile before the implementation. Choose one of the approaches compared; if the owner chose another approach for a decision of a design card, choose that one for that decision, and if the owner changed the acceptance, write it as changed; say in what point it beats each of the others, covering every one not chosen. If only a measurement can decide, measure first and judge the results yourself; if you measured, say how the results shaped the choice, and if not, why no measurement was needed. Then write the design itself: how it solves the problem, until it is clear, with code before and after and diagrams if useful; for a change to language rules, a checker or a library interface, give the code after the change and show how the problem's example is accepted after it; then where it changes, what it leaves out, and its constraints and pitfalls. If the design tree must change (the design paths the project's configuration names, such as design/), change the nodes in this round as the design tree rules say and commit them locally, then write the design card: one section per decision added, changed or removed, before, after and why, at least three approaches compared, the chosen one the recommendation and why each other was not chosen; how sure you are, on what grounds, and what would overturn it; provisional or to check for what cannot be settled; if the tree does not change, say why. Write the acceptance conditions to test at the end, each one sentence of plain language, saying whether a test or a measurement meets it; if they are locked already, write them as locked, and if you think they must change, first ask the advisor with the kind acceptance_change and write them as the reply says. If you cannot choose, ask, with one point design_undecided saying where it is stuck and what is missing to decide. When designing again after sub-items were split off: the design card still covers the whole work, and each decision says who carries it, this work itself or which sub-item; the branch keeps only the nodes this work carries itself and drops those given to sub-items. prompt: You only write tests: change only files in the test paths the project's configuration names, not the implementation; if you think the implementation is wrong, write a test that turns red, and the engineer fixes it. Every acceptance condition must be met by a test: one the engineer wrote that really tests the condition can be used as it is; otherwise write one. Then dig for corner cases; if the project's configuration names places to attack, attack them. Each test names the independent reference its verdict rests on, such as a specification, or an established implementation the project is compared with. New tests are of two kinds, handed in apart: new-behaviour tests test what this change brings, so they should fail before the change, or what they test does not exist before it; old-behaviour tests guard old behaviour the change must not alter, so they should pass before and after it; for an optimization or a refactoring, for instance, they check the meaning against the reference. Tests the engineer added go by the kind the engineer gave in the test changes. Run every new test, the engineer's and yours, once after the change with ci and once before it with ci_before: for the run before, the engine puts the test files on the code before the change, so you need not set it up.
